targeted_current_date_refresh.scope: InclusiveHAR article/dataset citation-use search plus claim-collision search for ability-associated population shift, domain generalization benchmarks, foundation models, factorization, and subject-invariant contrastive learning.
targeted_current_date_refresh.outcome: No InclusiveHAR downstream use or collision with the complete narrowed benchmark combination was verified. Nine close benchmark, population-shift, factorization, and contrastive-learning predecessors were added. The benchmark gate remains narrowly scoped; the completed MoRe-HAR model gate is closed as not supported.

scope: Primary papers, official proceedings or publisher pages, official repositories, and versioned dataset records inspected for Stage 1 claim and novelty gating.

evidence_labels.V: verified in an inspected primary or official source
evidence_labels.N: scoped negative search, not proof of absence
evidence_labels.NR: not reported or not verified in the inspected source

novelty_gate.model_result_boundary: The consumed locked target evaluation found compact DANN mean participant macro-F1 0.6808438 versus 0.6353323 for full MoRe-HAR. The preregistered mean and joint lower-tail improvement conditions both failed; no positive model-novelty claim is supported.
novelty_gate.candidate_contribution: An auditable participant-exclusive, released-block, one-way ability-associated population-shift benchmark on InclusiveHAR v4, with source-only model selection, explicit activity-realization ontology, matched strong baselines, participant-level lower-tail and calibration evidence, explicit unrecoverable hidden-trial-boundary risk, and a one-time target evaluation.
novelty_gate.caveat: The negative search is bounded to the recorded sources and queries through 2026-08-24. Indexing lag, incomplete full-text coverage, and unavailable automated Google Scholar access require a fresh submission-time search.

inclusivehar_citation_search.result: No post-release citing or using paper was verified in the searched sources through the targeted current-date refresh.

works.title: InclusiveHAR: A smartphone-based dataset for human activity recognition across diverse physical abilities
works.key_boundary: The paper already reports an author-described non-disabled-only training scenario, but split and target provenance are insufficient to verify a participant/trial-exclusive locked zero-shot protocol.

works.title: Human Activity Recognition Using Smartphones
works.key_boundary: Conventional 30-participant population and subject-separated official split; no disability metadata, and stairs/body-acceleration semantics are not automatically compatible with InclusiveHAR. The current catalog's CC BY 4.0 label conflicts with the embedded Version 1.0 non-commercial notice; both must be preserved as unresolved and the data must not be redistributed or relicensed.

works.title: Promoting fairness in activity recognition algorithms for patient's monitoring and evaluation systems in healthcare
works.key_boundary: Direct disability/fairness prior using Kinect skeleton shoulder exercises; not smartphone inertial or a locked source-only population-shift benchmark.

works.title: HAROOD: A Benchmark for Out-of-distribution Generalization in Sensor-based Human Activity Recognition
works.key_boundary: Preempts a generic HAR OOD benchmark claim; it has no ability-defined target, and oracle model selection is diagnostic.

works.title: BenchHAR: Benchmarking Self-Supervised Learning for Generalizable Sensor-based Activity Recognition
works.key_boundary: Preempts a generic SSL-generalization benchmark; no ability-defined cohort or participant lower-tail/calibration endpoint.

works.title: WHAR Arena: Benchmarking the State of the Art in Efficient Wearable Human Activity Recognition
works.key_boundary: Preempts generic standardized accuracy-efficiency comparison; no ability-defined one-way target.

works.title: ZeroHAR: Sensor Context Augments Zero-Shot Wearable Action Recognition
works.key_boundary: Preempts a generic zero-shot inertial HAR claim, but its zero-shot variable is the unseen activity class rather than target-participant supervision under a fixed shared ontology.

works.title: Generalizable Sensor-Based Activity Recognition via Categorical Concept Invariant Learning
works.key_boundary: Direct predecessor for category-conditioned invariant feature/logit learning; must be compared with MoRe-HAR.

works.title: In Shift and In Variance: Assessing the Robustness of HAR Deep Learning Models Against Variability
works.key_boundary: Direct prior for person/device/position/orientation shift, but not ability-associated source-to-target generalization.

works.title: STORM: Hardware-Aware Tiny Transformer Co-Design for Low-Power Inertial Human Activity Recognition
works.key_boundary: Preempts generic tiny-Transformer, sensor-fault, and edge-co-design claims; ability by reliability remains secondary.

works.title: Rotation-Invariant Multi-IMU Activity Recognition under Independent Per-Location Orientation Shifts
works.key_boundary: Preempts exact rotation-invariant multi-IMU novelty; not an ability-defined shift study.

works.title: Inertia-1: An Open Exploration of Wearable Motion Foundation Models
works.key_boundary: Preempts a generic wearable foundation-model-scale study; its pretraining scale is out of scope and it has no ability-defined target.

works.title: AnyMo: Geometry-Aware Setup-Agnostic Modeling of Human Motion in the Wild
works.key_boundary: Preempts generic setup-agnostic, cross-device, wearable-foundation, and zero-shot-recognition claims. AnyMo Bench is subject-exclusive but has no ability-defined target or one-way non-disabled-to-disabled protocol.

works.title: LITEWAY: LIghtweight HAR via Temporal Efficient highWAY
works.key_boundary: Preempts a generic lightweight fully convolutional HAR architecture claim; its closest UCI interface uses nine channels and overlapping windows, it does not study ability-associated shift, and audited source reuse is blocked by absent software licensing.

works.title: Learning Disentangled Behaviour Patterns for Wearable-based Human Activity Recognition
works.key_boundary: High conceptual collision: BPD already separates activity behaviour from personal style/environmental nuisance and reports participant-level F1.

works.title: CMD-HAR: Cross-Modal Disentanglement for Wearable Human Activity Recognition
works.key_boundary: Further invalidates generic disentanglement novelty; ratio-only split documentation does not establish subject exclusivity for all datasets.

works.title: Human Activity Recognition Dataset for Pedestrians with Mobility Disabilities
works.key_boundary: Strong mobility-aid HAR benchmark with 120 participants and user-independent evaluation, but activities are simulated modes/aids rather than same-activity generalization to an independently recruited disabled cohort.

works.title: Human Activity Recognition from Smartphone Sensor Data for Clinical Trials
works.key_boundary: Includes healthy controls and people with MS, but GaitLab development mixes both cohorts and the full everyday-activity endpoint is evaluated only on healthy Roche participants.

works.title: Activity Recognition for Persons With Stroke Using Mobile Phone Technology
works.key_boundary: Direct smartphone healthy-to-stroke transfer precedent; rules out first healthy-to-disabled smartphone evaluation.

works.title: Activity Recognition in Individuals Walking With Assistive Devices: Benefits of Device-Specific Models
works.key_boundary: Direct healthy-global-to-assistive-device-user evaluation; rules out first assistive-device or healthy-to-disabled transfer claim.

works.title: Human Activity Recognition of Individuals with Lower Limb Amputation in Free-Living Conditions: A Pilot Study
works.key_boundary: Direct non-impaired-to-lower-limb-amputee transfer failure; strongly narrows cross-ability novelty language.

works.title: Latent Independent Excitation for Generalizable Sensor-based Cross-Person Activity Recognition
works.key_boundary: Closest factorization predecessor: target-free cross-person HAR explicitly separates domain-agnostic activity representations from domain-specific person representations and reduces their dependence.

works.title: Domain Generalization for Activity Recognition via Adaptive Feature Fusion
works.key_boundary: Target-free cross-person predecessor that fuses domain-invariant and source-domain-specific representations; preempts the generic invariant/specific decomposition principle.

works.title: A benchmark for domain adaptation and generalization in smartphone-based human activity recognition
works.key_boundary: Preempts a generic smartphone domain-adaptation/domain-generalization benchmark claim, but has no ability-defined source/target population.

works.title: Assessing Distribution Shift in Human Activity Recognition for Domain Generalization
works.key_boundary: Preempts broad user-behaviour/activity-realization and generic DG-benchmark framing. V1 selects reported models using combined validation and held-out test-domain performance, so its rankings are not locked-target evidence.

works.title: HARBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Foundation Models in Sensor-based Human Activity Recognition
works.key_boundary: Current foundation-model benchmark prior with domain, position, few-shot, and zero-shot tracks; distinct from BenchHAR and not an ability-defined one-way target.

works.title: Age Matters: Evaluating Cross Population Generalization in Wearable Sensor Based Human Activity Recognition
works.key_boundary: Direct younger-versus-older demographic population-shift precedent. It does not study disability or InclusiveHAR, and accessible metadata does not resolve cross-dataset device/protocol confounding.

works.title: ContrastSense: Domain-invariant Contrastive Learning for In-the-Wild Wearable Sensing
works.key_boundary: Direct predecessor for user/device-domain invariant contrastive representations under source-label scarcity; no ability-defined target.

works.title: Subject Invariant Contrastive Learning for Human Activity Recognition
works.key_boundary: Direct subject-invariant contrastive-loss predecessor; exact cross-subject split construction is underreported in the inspected sources.

works.title: Towards User-Generalizable Wearable-Sensor-Based Human Activity Recognition: A Multi-Task Contrastive Learning Approach
works.key_boundary: Near-exact component predecessor: same-activity/different-user positives and different-activity/same-user hard negatives under user-disjoint evaluation.
